The feeder identifier, combined with substation, pinpoints a specific geographic segment of the electrical grid. With only 70 housing units in this segment, the feeder number acts as a quasi-identifier that can narrow down to a small, identifiable group of consumers. Under data protection principles, this constitutes a location-based identifier that could enable re-identification of individuals within that grid segment.

The substation identifier identifies a specific physical location in the electrical grid infrastructure. Combined with the feeder number, it creates a precise geographic reference that can identify a small community of consumers. This is a location-based quasi-identifier that, in the context of a small service area, could lead to re-identification of individuals.

The date column is a temporal reference that does not by itself constitute personal data. While it adds temporal specificity to the dataset, it is a standard reporting dimension and does not directly identify any individual. In the context of aggregate grid-level data, the date alone does not enable re-identification.

This is an aggregate count of housing units in the grid segment. It does not identify any specific individual or household. As a statistical aggregate, it does not constitute personal data under data protection principles. The value (70-72 units) is too coarse to identify any specific person.
